title: When the Orbit Sings
premise: Emrys Crane, the last human technician aboard the derelict relay station Vesper, has spent six years quietly archiving the final transmissions of Meridian Colony before its 'scheduled decommission'—a euphemism she suspects hides something darker. When the colony's surviving children, scattered across the system in foster care, begin sharing an identical dream of a red-lit corridor and a song with no source, Emrys realizes their minds recorded what the corporation erased. To prove the massacre happened, she must rebuild the deleted logs from fragments hidden in her own maintenance routines, expose the cover-up, and give the children back their memory—knowing the corporation will erase her the moment she becomes visible. In the end, she broadcasts the children's dream-song across every open channel, forcing the truth into public record at the cost of her own anonymity, and the found family she never meant to make carries her name forward.
about_author: Rosalind Galloway is the pen name of a former radio engineer who spent a decade maintaining remote transmission sites in the northern latitudes. She writes quiet, aching science fiction about the people machines forget.

chapters.title: The Quiet Hours
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Six years alone on the relay station, Emrys maintains her routines and secretly archives Meridian's final transmissions, which the official record calls a peaceful decommission. A routine signal ping carries an impossible fragment: a child's voice singing a melody she's never heard but somehow recognizes. The beat is loneliness cracking into unease—the first hint that the silence she's curated is a lie.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Dream
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, with interludes from eleven-year-old Sefa, one of the dreamers. Sefa contacts the station after tracing the dream-song's source to Emrys's relay. The children all dream the red corridor and the song; their foster records were scrubbed of Meridian. Emrys realizes their shared memory is living evidence. Rising tension: she chooses to respond, abandoning invisibility for the first time.

chapters.title: Every Record Says Otherwise
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Corporate auditors arrive to decommission the station early—the song's broadcast triggered an automated flag. Emrys races to reconstruct the deleted massacre logs from checksum fragments buried in her own maintenance scripts while the auditors close in. Climax: she finds the kill order, timestamped and signed, just as they cut her uplink. The beat is terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, closing with Sefa's. With minutes before the station goes dark, Emrys transmits the reconstructed logs and the children's dream-song on every open channel—unencrypted, undeniable. The auditors seize the station, but the truth is already loose; Sefa leads the dreamers in singing it publicly. Resolution: Emrys loses her invisibility and her station but gains a family, her name carried in the song.
